biological_question: Does isolation-generated visitor assembly rotate the joint local selection field toward lower floral investment and stronger reproductive assurance, and when does that shift become an actual sign reversal and realized two-trait response?

estimands.beta: Rare-mutant invasion selection gradient: derivative of log tagged-mutant parental gene-copy-equivalent contribution with respect to mutant floral investment i and assurance a, evaluated at mutant=resident while resident environment is held fixed.
estimands.parental_gene_copy_fitness: 0.5*(maternal outcross seeds + paternal outcross seeds) + viable selfed seeds; selfed offspring count as two transmitted parental gametes and therefore one whole parental genome equivalent.
estimands.history_beta: Arithmetic mean of annual beta vectors across the 200 exogenous visitor states at a fixed resident trait state.
estimands.price_response: Exact one-generation first-moment response from individual parental genome-equivalent fitness: Delta zbar = Cov(z,w)/mean(w), evaluated separately for i and a.
estimands.lande_response: G beta using the full 2x2 standing covariance matrix, including the off-diagonal term.
estimands.realized_trajectory: Finite-ABM terminal trait change after 200 reproductive years, evaluated separately from beta and one-generation response.

delayed_zero_cost_control.role: negative_control_for_inference; upward assurance selection is structurally favoured when unused ovules remain and is not syndrome evidence

selection_shift.target_quadrant: far-minus-near beta_i negative and beta_a positive
selection_shift.confidence: paired_history bootstrap 95%, 1999 resamples, RNG seed 1004; both component intervals must exclude zero in target directions

actual_assurance_sign_reversal.definition: near beta_a <= -0.02 and far beta_a >= +0.02 within the same history

multivariate_response.standardization: divide each one-generation response component by its parental trait SD
multivariate_response.syndrome_quadrant: Delta i negative and Delta a positive

realized_finite_abm.history_branching: within one setting, both endpoint classes each occur in >=10% of eligible histories
realized_finite_abm.eligibility: occupied at baseline and endpoint; occupancy always reported unconditionally

predictions: Far-minus-near beta shift points toward lower investment and higher assurance in all four settings, but the delayed zero-cost control is not inferential evidence.
Actual assurance sign reversal is expected only in at least one identifying setting with prior selfing, pollen discounting, or direct assurance cost.
The full G matrix can rotate G beta away from beta; therefore beta-shift and response-shift conclusions are adjudicated separately.

Negative correlational selection between investment and assurance is expected when increased investment raises outcrossing, but fixed inbreeding depression excludes purging feedback and limits claims about classical mating-system bistability.

Alternative endpoints or history-dependent branching, if present under the frozen endpoint rule, can be promoted as a mechanistic repeatability result; otherwise the extension remains a supporting syndrome-shift result.
claim_boundaries: No purging or evolution of inbreeding depression; delta is fixed.
No claim that a monomorphic population derivative in assurance is a selection gradient.
No universal island selfing syndrome claim.
No natural-island calibration of synthetic distance or cost coefficients.
No promotion into locked submission surfaces until all three layers are evaluated under this contract.
